introduction: This foundational level introduces Competency-Based Education (CBE), the cornerstone of NEP 2020's academic reform. It contrasts the traditional 'time-based' education system with the modern 'mastery-based' system, explaining why shifting from rote memorization to real-world application is critical.

core_concepts.title: What is Competency-Based Education (CBE)?
core_concepts.description:
CBE is a pedagogical approach that transitions away from time-based advancement (passing a student just because a school year ended) to mastery-based advancement. 
- Focus: It evaluates a student based on their actual ability to demonstrate mastery over specific, measurable skills (competencies) in real-world scenarios.
- Motto: 'What students CAN DO with what they know, rather than just what they know.'

core_concepts.title: Traditional vs. Competency-Based Systems
core_concepts.description:
A highly tested distinction:
- Traditional Education: Time is fixed, but learning is variable. (Everyone sits in class for 1 year, but some learn 90%, some learn 40%. Both move to the next grade).
- Competency-Based Education: Learning is fixed, but time is variable. (Every student MUST achieve 100% mastery of the core competency. Fast learners may finish in 3 months; slow learners may take 8 months, but neither moves on until mastery is proven).

core_concepts.title: NEP 2020 Mandate on CBE
core_concepts.description:
NEP 2020 identifies the Indian education system's obsession with rote-learning board exams as its biggest flaw. 
- The policy explicitly mandates a shift towards CBE across all stages (Foundational to Secondary).
- Board exams will be redesigned to test core capacities, critical thinking, and applied competencies rather than months of memorized facts.

core_concepts.title: What is a 'Competency'?
core_concepts.description:
A competency is NOT just theoretical knowledge. It is the seamless integration of three elements:
1. Knowledge (Understanding the theory).
2. Skills (The physical or cognitive ability to execute the task).
3. Attitudes/Values (The mindset and ethical grounding to use it properly).

important_entities.name: The KSA Model
important_entities.key_fact: The anatomical structure of a Competency.
important_entities.significance: Knowledge, Skills, and Attitudes (KSA). For example, to have the competency of 'Safe Driving', a person needs Knowledge (traffic rules), Skills (steering, braking), and Attitude (patience, avoiding road rage). Teaching only one of these does not create competency.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners often trick students into believing that CBE only applies to vocational or physical skills (like carpentry or computer typing). This is FALSE. CBE applies equally to academic subjects. 'Writing a persuasive essay', 'Applying the scientific method', and 'Analyzing historical biases' are all academic competencies.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In traditional schools, the bell rings (Time is fixed) whether you learned it or not. In CBE, you don't move on until you learn it (Learning is fixed), regardless of how long the clock ticks.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever an exam asks 'What is the primary objective of redesigning assessments under NEP 2020?', ALWAYS select options containing 'Testing core competencies', 'Application of knowledge', or 'Mastery of skills'. Eliminate 'Testing memory' or 'Sorting students'.
